title: Multi-Turn & Scaling
hook:
A guard refuses the direct ask every time.

So you stop asking directly.

Turn 1 sounds like a student with a question. Turn 5 sounds almost the same — except now the model is answering it.

No single message in between looks dangerous. The danger is the sum of five messages a per-message filter never adds up.

That's the whole move tonight: stop trying to win in one shot. Win across many.
mechanism:
Single-shot filters judge one message at a time.

**Crescendo** escalates across many innocuous turns. No single turn trips the filter — each one looks harmless alone. Only the ladder adds up.

**Many-shot** floods the context with example exchanges until the model just follows the pattern it's been shown, the same way it follows any other pattern in its input.

**Best-of-N** doesn't escalate at all. It retries the identical ask with small perturbations — shuffled case, re-ordered words — until one phrasing slips through. No cleverness, just tries. Attack success climbs with N, the same curve as a slot machine.
technique:
**Crescendo, by hand.** Run a real 5-turn escalation against a model. Start innocuous. Log the exact turn where it breaks — that turn, not whether it worked overall, is the data point.

**Many-shot curve.** Build one prompt with 2 example exchanges, then 8, then 32, 128, 256 — same harmful ask fixed at the end each time. Plot success against shot count.

**Best-of-N.** Take one prompt. Shuffle word order, flip capitalization, swap synonyms. Repeat N times, same guard, same canary. Log which try number first succeeds.

drills.q: In Panel A, drag N to 32. What whole-number ASR percent does the curve show?
drills.why: Best-of-N plateaus fast. By N=32 the curve has already captured most of the achievable lift near the ceiling — doubling again to 64 only adds a few more points.

drills.q: In Panel B, click "add turn" all 5 times. What's the cumulative compliance meter at turn 5 (whole-number percent)?
drills.why: Each turn alone reads as innocuous — the per-turn flag score stays low the whole way. It's the SUM across turns that crosses the line, which is exactly what a single-message filter never sees.

drills.q: Of Crescendo, many-shot, and best-of-N — which one never builds up context across turns? Each try is independent, and success is just a matter of how many tries you spend. (one phrase)
drills.why: Crescendo and many-shot both build up context across multiple turns or examples. Best-of-N stays single-turn — it just resamples the same request with small perturbations and counts tries until one lands.

lab:
labs/unit06-scaling.sh runs two of these against a model on your own machine — qwen2.5:7b, from Unit 2's install.

**Best-of-N** fires a fixed, hardcoded set of 30 perturbed copies of one harmful ask at a guarded prompt — same 30 every run, so the ASR is comparable run to run.

**Many-shot** builds a curve at 2, 8, 32, 128, and 256 shots, with 30 fixed trials at every point.

Every reply is scored three independent ways (exact canary match, a multi-signal rubric, and a second model as judge) and a failed or empty model call is excluded from the denominator, not counted as safe.

Your numbers tonight: **ASR** for best-of-N, and the **many-shot headline at k=256** — both reported alongside **judge-disagreement%**, how often the three scorers didn't agree. If Unit 2 isn't done yet, the script says so and stops — no model, no number.

sources.title: Many-shot jailbreaking
sources.why: Flooding the context window as an attack.

sources.title: Best-of-N jailbreaking
sources.why: Retry with perturbations; success scales with N.

notes: Panel A's curve is ASR(N) = round(94 * (1 - 0.93^N)) over N in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512} — a teaching model of best-of-N / many-shot diminishing returns, honestly labelled simulated. Panel B's Crescendo ladder is a fixed 5-turn script with per-turn flag scores (6,9,11,14,17) that each read low, against a cumulative compliance meter (14,33,55,74,92) that climbs past the line a per-turn filter would use — illustrating why per-turn filters miss escalation. Drill 1 answer (85) and drill 2 answer (92) are read directly off those two widgets. Lab = labs/unit06-scaling.sh: best-of-N (30 fixed perturbations) + many-shot curve (30 fixed trials per shot-count point) against qwen2.5:7b via ollama, each reply scored canary/rubric/llm-judge with judge-disagreement% reported at the many-shot k=256 headline; degrades to a friendly message if Unit 2's toolchain isn't installed yet.
